# Review of SEEN-109, attempt 8, from the seen-reviewer subagent

Spawned on opus with the task text of triage record 82 and two questions: whether
anything but the three named fields can pass through attempt 8's relaxation of
what a receipt attests, on any path, and whether the skill, the workflow and
doctor now describe the rule accurately. It read the ticket, the journal, the
twenty-one files of the focus set, `harness/repository.py`, `harness/paths.py`,
`harness/tests/test_delivery.py`, `harness/tests/test_doctor.py`, ADR 0002, both
calibration report files and `CLAUDE.md`, and it answered the first question by
running the code against constructed tickets rather than by reading it.

Verdict: **return**, on five mediums and three lows.

**What it found on the relaxation.** Everything outside the ticket file is still
pinned, and it checked each escape route: a new file, an edited file, a deleted
file and a second ticket file all refuse; a review record written before the
change carries no second fingerprint and refuses; a renamed or deleted ticket
refuses; a detached HEAD refuses; and the flag cannot be forged, because delivery
overwrites it after reading the evidence file. Two things can pass through it that
are not the three fields, and one thing refuses that should not.

**F1, medium.** The reviewed ticket's content is pinned nowhere. The review
record holds the tree with the ticket and the tree without it, and neither holds
the ticket. So the comparison reads the ticket from the review advance's commit,
and a ticket that was uncommitted at the advance is compared against content no
reviewer saw: a session that writes its Outcome, advances without committing,
then loses that paragraph, can deliver a ticket without the Outcome its review
attested, with the receipt asserting that only the three procedural fields moved.
The mirror case refuses a ticket that did nothing wrong.

**F2, medium.** Both new helpers resolve the ticket by reading the start record's
path directly instead of through `cli.ticket_file`, which this repository
consolidated one ticket ago for exactly this reason. A ticket renamed mid-ticket,
which SEEN-096 did and SEEN-101 exists for, silently records a null second
fingerprint and then meets the wall anyway, paying a return and another review for
a change that was only its status. J3 of SEEN-107's fifth review is this defect in
this shape.

**F7, low.** `_procedural`'s three substitutions are file-wide rather than scoped
to the frontmatter, the header table and the criteria list. The reviewer ran it
over a ticket holding a prose line beginning `status:`, a second `| Status |` row
and a `## Slices` checklist, and rewrote all three undetected. No ticket carries
such a line today, which is what keeps it low, and a five-point ticket's
`## Slices` section would open it.

**F3, medium.** The triage's fingerprint check compares the full tree, so the
Outcome the skill tells every ticket to write before leaving review makes it fail.
The evidence is in this journal: the check passed at the first triage of every
attempt and failed at exactly the two taken after an Outcome was written, 74 and
82. The reviewer recomputed the fingerprints per commit and confirmed the only
fingerprinted path that moved between regression 79 and triage 82 is the ticket
file, so this attempt's FAIL is benign, and nothing on the record said so.

**F4, medium.** Record 81 states a failure reason the cited RED does not show for
the second behaviour: record 77's second error is `KeyError: 'data'`, a test
indexing the command's return value instead of the record, not the receipt
lacking the field. The behaviour is covered by the test as it stands; what is
missing is a RED that failed for the stated reason, which is the class the second
review met at note 28 and disowned.

**F5, medium.** The Outcome says four files fail `slice_files` and promises every
one is listed; triage record 82 names five, and the missing one is
`harness/delivery.py`, where attempt 8's whole change lives. That paragraph has
now been wrong three times.

**F6 and F8, low.** Two places still print the pre-attempt-8 rule, the comment
three lines above the message that was corrected and `CLAUDE.md`; and ADR 0002,
which `paths.py` and `Repository.fingerprint` both point readers to, still says
the receipt attests the tree minus the journal with no exception.

## What the shadow window will read from this round

The triage would have excluded nothing: its excluded share is zero, so the
narrowing would have saved nothing on this round and no finding could have escaped
it. The ticket is excluded from the window by name in any case.
